1: """
2: WebSocket-based notification server with a Redis pub/sub message backbone.
3: 
4: Accepts WebSocket connections, assigns each client a unique ID, broadcasts
5: messages to all connected clients, handles clean disconnects, and exposes REST
6: endpoints for health, channels, and message history.
7: 
8: Message backbone
9: ----------------
10: Messages are distributed over Redis pub/sub channels. A server publishes every
11: broadcast to a Redis channel and every server instance runs a subscriber that
12: delivers the message to its own connected clients. This lets multiple server
13: instances share a single Redis backbone. When Redis is unavailable the server
14: delivers locally, so it keeps working without a broker.
15: 
16: Client connection state (client IDs and their channel subscriptions) is
17: mirrored into Redis when a broker is available, so the state survives a server
18: restart.
19: 
20: Persistence
21: -----------
22: Every broadcast and direct message is stored in SQLite so a history can be
23: served back through ``GET /messages``.
24: 
25: Configuration
26: -------------
27: ``REDIS_URL``    optional Redis connection URL for the pub/sub backbone.
28: ``DATABASE_URL`` optional SQLite path (or ``sqlite:///...`` URL) for history.
29: 
30: Clients can subscribe to named channels (e.g. ``"alerts"``, ``"system"``,
31: ``"chat"``). Messages that carry a ``channel`` field are delivered only to the
32: clients subscribed to that channel; messages without a channel still broadcast
33: to all connected clients.
34: 
35: Message format (JSON)::
36: 
37:     {"type": str, "payload": dict, "timestamp": str}
38: 
39: Supported types: ``"broadcast"``, ``"direct"``, ``"system"``, ``"subscribe"``,
40: ``"unsubscribe"``.
41: 
42: REST endpoints::
43: 
44:     GET /health                          connected client count
45:     GET /channels                        active channels and subscriber counts
46:     GET /channels/{name}/subscribers     subscriber IDs for a channel
47:     GET /messages?limit=50&offset=0      persisted message history
48: """

107: # ── Pub/Sub backbone ────────────────────────────────────────────────

109: class Broker:
110:     """
111:     Pub/sub message backbone.
112: 
113:     When a ``redis_client`` is supplied (or ``REDIS_URL`` is set) messages are
114:     published to Redis channels and each server runs a subscriber task that
115:     delivers them to its local clients, letting multiple server instances share
116:     a single backbone. Without Redis the server falls back to a no-op broker and
117:     delivers locally, so it keeps working with no broker running.
118:     """
119: 
120:     def __init__(self, redis_client=None) -> None:
121:         self.redis_client = redis_client
122:         self._pubsub = None
123:         self._subscribed: set[str] = set()
124:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
125:         self._connected = False
126: 
127:     @property
128:     def redis_enabled(self) -> bool:
129:         return self.redis_client is not None
130: 
131:     async def connect(self) -> None:
132:         """Prepare the broker for use, degrading gracefully to in-memory."""
133:         if self._connected:
134:             return
135:         if self.redis_client is not None:
136:             try:
137:                 await self.redis_client.ping()
138:             except Exception:
139:                 self.redis_client = None
140:         self._connected = True
141:         if self.redis_client is not None:
142:             self._pubsub = self.redis_client.pubsub()
143: 
144:     async def subscribe(self, channel: str) -> None:
145:         await self.connect()
146:         if self.redis_client is None:
147:             return
148:         with self._lock:
149:             if channel in self._subscribed:
150:                 return
151:             self._subscribed.add(channel)
152:         await self._pubsub.subscribe(channel)
153: 
154:     async def unsubscribe(self, channel: str) -> None:
155:         await self.connect()
156:         if self.redis_client is None:
157:             return
158:         with self._lock:
159:             if channel not in self._subscribed:
160:                 return
161:             self._subscribed.discard(channel)
162:         await self._pubsub.unsubscribe(channel)
163: 
164:     def channels_subscribed(self) -> set[str]:
165:         with self._lock:
166:             return set(self._subscribed)
167: 
168:     async def publish(self, channel: str, payload: dict) -> None:
169:         """Publish a message dict to a channel."""
170:         await self.connect()
171:         if self.redis_client is None:
172:             return
173:         await self.redis_client.publish(channel, json.dumps(payload))
174: 
175:     async def next_message(self):
176:         """
177:         Return the next ``(channel, data)`` from Redis, or ``None`` when nothing
178:         is pending. Polls so cancellation during event loop shutdown is clean.
179:         """
180:         await self.connect()
181:         if self.redis_client is None:
182:             await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
183:             return None
184:         msg = await self._pubsub.get_message(ignore_subscribe_messages=True)
185:         if msg is None:
186:             await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
187:             return None
188:         channel = _decode(msg.get("channel"))
189:         data = _decode(msg.get("data"))
190:         if channel is None or data is None:
191:             return None
192:         return channel, data

211: # ── Persistence ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

213: class MessageStore:
214:     """
215:     SQLite-backed history for messages.
216: 
217:     The ``messages`` table holds ``id``, ``channel``, ``type``, ``payload``
218:     (JSON-encoded) and ``timestamp``. A single connection guarded by a lock is
219:     reused so in-memory databases (``:memory:``) work correctly.
220:     """
221: 
222:     def __init__(self, database: str | None = None) -> None:
223:         self.database = database or _database_url()
224:         self._path = self._resolve_path(self.database)
225:         self._conn = sqlite3.connect(self._path, check_same_thread=False)
226:         self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
227:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
228:         self._init_schema()
229:         weakref.finalize(self, self._close_connection, self._conn)
230: 
231:     @staticmethod
232:     def _close_connection(conn) -> None:
233:         try:
234:             conn.close()
235:         except Exception:
236:             pass
237: 
238:     @staticmethod
239:     def _resolve_path(database: str | None) -> str:
240:         if not database:
241:             return ":memory:"
242:         if database.startswith("sqlite:///"):
243:             return database[len("sqlite:///"):]
244:         if database.startswith("sqlite://"):
245:             return database[len("sqlite://"):] or ":memory:"
246:         return database
247: 
248:     def _init_schema(self) -> None:
249:         with self._lock:
250:             self._conn.execute(
251:                 """
252:                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
253:                     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
254:                     channel TEXT,
255:                     type TEXT NOT NULL,
256:                     payload TEXT NOT NULL,
257:                     timestamp TEXT NOT NULL
258:                 )
259:                 """
260:             )
261:             self._conn.commit()
262: 
263:     def save(self, message: dict, channel: str | None = None) -> int:
264:         """Persist a message dict. Returns the new row id."""
265:         with self._lock:
266:             cur = self._conn.execute(
267:                 "INSERT INTO messages (channel, type, payload, timestamp) "
268:                 "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
269:                 (
270:                     channel,
271:                     message["type"],
272:                     json.dumps(message["payload"]),
273:                     message["timestamp"],
274:                 ),
275:             )
276:             self._conn.commit()
277:             return cur.lastrowid
278: 
279:     def list(self, limit: int = 50, offset: int = 0) -> list[dict]:
280:         """Return stored messages ordered by id (oldest first)."""
281:         limit = max(0, int(limit))
282:         offset = max(0, int(offset))
283:         with self._lock:
284:             rows = self._conn.execute(
285:                 "SELECT id, channel, type, payload, timestamp "
286:                 "FROM messages ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
287:                 (limit, offset),
288:             ).fetchall()
289:         out = []
290:         for row in rows:
291:             entry = dict(row)
292:             try:
293:                 entry["payload"] = json.loads(entry["payload"])
294:             except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
295:                 pass
296:             out.append(entry)
297:         return out
298: 
299:     def count(self) -> int:
300:         with self._lock:
301:             row = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages").fetchone()
302:             return int(row[0])
303: 
304:     def close(self) -> None:
305:         with self._lock:
306:             self._conn.close()

309: # ── Redis-backed client connection state ───────────────────────────

311: class ConnectionStore:
312:     """
313:     Client connection state, mirrored to Redis when available.
314: 
315:     Client IDs and their channel subscriptions are recorded here so the state
316:     survives a server restart. Falls back to an in-memory map when no Redis
317:     connection is available.
318:     """
319: 
320:     CLIENTS_KEY = "ntf:clients"
321: 
322:     def __init__(self, redis_client=None) -> None:
323:         self.redis_client = redis_client
324:         self._memory: dict[str, dict] = {}
325:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
326: 
327:     @property
328:     def redis_enabled(self) -> bool:
329:         return self.redis_client is not None
330: 
331:     @staticmethod
332:     def _client_key(client_id: str) -> str:
333:         return f"ntf:client:{client_id}"
334: 
335:     async def register(self, client_id: str) -> None:
336:         if self.redis_client is not None:
337:             await self.redis_client.sadd(self.CLIENTS_KEY, client_id)
338:             await self.redis_client.hset(
339:                 self._client_key(client_id), "channels", "[]"
340:             )
341:         else:
342:             with self._lock:
343:                 self._memory[client_id] = {"channels": set()}
344: 
345:     async def unregister(self, client_id: str) -> None:
346:         if self.redis_client is not None:
347:             await self.redis_client.srem(self.CLIENTS_KEY, client_id)
348:             await self.redis_client.delete(self._client_key(client_id))
349:         else:
350:             with self._lock:
351:                 self._memory.pop(client_id, None)
352: 
353:     async def add_channel(self, client_id: str, channel: str) -> None:
354:         if self.redis_client is not None:
355:             channels = await self.channels_for(client_id)
356:             if channel not in channels:
357:                 channels.append(channel)
358:                 await self.redis_client.hset(
359:                     self._client_key(client_id),
360:                     "channels",
361:                     json.dumps(channels),
362:                 )
363:         else:
364:             with self._lock:
365:                 entry = self._memory.get(client_id)
366:                 if entry is not None:
367:                     entry["channels"].add(channel)
368: 
369:     async def remove_channel(self, client_id: str, channel: str) -> None:
370:         if self.redis_client is not None:
371:             channels = await self.channels_for(client_id)
372:             if channel in channels:
373:                 channels.remove(channel)
374:                 await self.redis_client.hset(
375:                     self._client_key(client_id),
376:                     "channels",
377:                     json.dumps(channels),
378:                 )
379:         else:
380:             with self._lock:
381:                 entry = self._memory.get(client_id)
382:                 if entry is not None:
383:                     entry["channels"].discard(channel)
384: 
385:     async def channels_for(self, client_id: str) -> list[str]:
386:         if self.redis_client is not None:
387:             raw = await self.redis_client.hget(
388:                 self._client_key(client_id), "channels"
389:             )
390:             if raw is None:
391:                 return []
392:             try:
393:                 return json.loads(_decode(raw))
394:             except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
395:                 return []
396:         with self._lock:
397:             entry = self._memory.get(client_id)
398:             return sorted(entry["channels"]) if entry else []
399: 
400:     async def clients(self) -> list[str]:
401:         if self.redis_client is not None:
402:             raw = await self.redis_client.smembers(self.CLIENTS_KEY)
403:             return sorted(_decode(c) for c in raw)
404:         with self._lock:
405:             return sorted(self._memory)

408: # ── Connection and channel registries ──────────────────────────────
409: 
410: class ClientRegistry:
411:     """
412:     Thread-safe registry mapping client IDs to their WebSocket connections.
413: 
414:     All operations are protected by a reentrant lock so the registry can be
415:     mutated from the asyncio event loop or from plain threads (e.g. the
416:     synchronous HTTP health check) without corruption.
417:     """
418: 
419:     def __init__(self) -> None:
420:         self._clients: dict[str, object] = {}
421:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
422: 
423:     def add(self, client_id: str, websocket: object) -> None:
424:         with self._lock:
425:             self._clients[client_id] = websocket
426: 
427:     def remove(self, client_id: str) -> object | None:
428:         with self._lock:
429:             return self._clients.pop(client_id, None)
430: 
431:     def get(self, client_id: str) -> object | None:
432:         with self._lock:
433:             return self._clients.get(client_id)
434: 
435:     def all(self) -> list[tuple[str, object]]:
436:         with self._lock:
437:             return list(self._clients.items())
438: 
439:     def count(self) -> int:
440:         with self._lock:
441:             return len(self._clients)
442:

444: class ChannelRegistry:
445:     """
446:     Thread-safe registry mapping channel names to the set of subscribed client
447:     IDs. A client may subscribe to any number of channels.
448:     """
449: 
450:     def __init__(self) -> None:
451:         self._channels: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
452:         self._lock = threading.RLock()
453: 
454:     def subscribe(self, channel: str, client_id: str) -> None:
455:         with self._lock:
456:             self._channels.setdefault(channel, set()).add(client_id)
457: 
458:     def unsubscribe(self, channel: str, client_id: str) -> None:
459:         with self._lock:
460:             members = self._channels.get(channel)
461:             if members is None:
462:                 return
463:             members.discard(client_id)
464:             if not members:
465:                 self._channels.pop(channel, None)
466: 
467:     def remove_client(self, client_id: str) -> None:
468:         with self._lock:
469:             empty = []
470:             for channel, members in self._channels.items():
471:                 members.discard(client_id)
472:                 if not members:
473:                     empty.append(channel)
474:             for channel in empty:
475:                 self._channels.pop(channel, None)
476: 
477:     def subscribers(self, channel: str) -> list[str]:
478:         with self._lock:
479:             return sorted(self._channels.get(channel, set()))
480: 
481:     def channels(self) -> dict[str, int]:
482:         with self._lock:
483:             return {name: len(members) for name, members in self._channels.items()}

486: # ── Server ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
487: 
488: class NotificationServer:
489:     """WebSocket notification server built on the ``websockets`` library."""
490: 
491:     def __init__(
492:         self,
493:         registry: ClientRegistry | None = None,
494:         channels: ChannelRegistry | None = None,
495:         broker: Broker | None = None,
496:         message_store: MessageStore | None = None,
497:         connection_store: ConnectionStore | None = None,
498:     ) -> None:
499:         self.registry = registry or ClientRegistry()
500:         self.channels = channels or ChannelRegistry()
501:         self.broker = broker or _make_default_broker()
502:         self.message_store = message_store or MessageStore()
503:         self.connection_store = connection_store or ConnectionStore()
504:         self._listener_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
505:         self._listener_started = False
506: 
507:     async def _ensure_listener(self) -> None:
508:         """
509:         Start the broker subscriber task (once). Only needed in Redis mode;
510:         without a broker messages are delivered inline during publishing.
511:         """
512:         if self._listener_started or not self.broker.redis_enabled:
513:             return
514:         self._listener_started = True
515:         await self.broker.subscribe(BROADCAST_CHANNEL)
516:         self._listener_task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
517:             self._run_listener()
518:         )
519: 
520:     async def _run_listener(self) -> None:
521:         """Consume messages from the backbone and deliver them locally."""
522:         while True:
523:             item = await self.broker.next_message()
524:             if item is None:
525:                 continue
526:             channel, data = item
527:             try:
528:                 json.loads(data)
529:             except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
530:                 continue
531:             if channel == BROADCAST_CHANNEL:
532:                 client_ids = [cid for cid, _ in self.registry.all()]
533:             else:
534:                 client_ids = self.channels.subscribers(channel)
535:             await self._deliver(data, client_ids)
536: 
537:     async def _sync_channel_subscriptions(self) -> None:
538:         """Subscribe the backbone to channels with local subscribers."""
539:         await self._ensure_listener()
540:         desired = {BROADCAST_CHANNEL, *self.channels.channels().keys()}
541:         current = self.broker.channels_subscribed()
542:         for channel in desired - current:
543:             await self.broker.subscribe(channel)
544:         for channel in current - desired:
545:             await self.broker.unsubscribe(channel)
546: 
547:     def close(self) -> None:
548:         """Cancel the broker subscriber task (used during shutdown)."""
549:         if self._listener_task is not None and not self._listener_task.done():
550:             self._listener_task.cancel()
551:         self._listener_task = None
552: 
553:     async def handler(self, websocket) -> None:
554:         """Handle a single WebSocket connection lifecycle."""
555:         await self._ensure_listener()
556:         client_id = self._new_client_id()
557:         self.registry.add(client_id, websocket)
558:         await self.connection_store.register(client_id)
559:         welcome = make_message(
560:             "system",
561:             {"client_id": client_id, "message": "connected"},
562:         )
563:         try:
564:             await websocket.send(json.dumps(welcome))
565:             async for raw in websocket:
566:                 await self._handle_message(client_id, websocket, raw)
567:         except ConnectionClosed:
568:             pass
569:         finally:
570:             self.registry.remove(client_id)

"""
WebSocket-based notification server with a Redis pub/sub message backbone.

Accepts WebSocket connections, assigns each client a unique ID, broadcasts
messages to all connected clients, handles clean disconnects, and exposes REST
endpoints for health, channels, and message history.

Message backbone
----------------
Messages are distributed over Redis pub/sub channels. A server publishes every
broadcast to a Redis channel and every server instance runs a subscriber that
delivers the message to its own connected clients. This lets multiple server
instances share a single Redis backbone. When Redis is unavailable the server
delivers locally, so it keeps working without a broker.

Client connection state (client IDs and their channel subscriptions) is
mirrored into Redis when a broker is available, so the state survives a server
restart.

@asynccontextmanager
async def running_server():
    server = NotificationServer()
    async with websockets.serve(
        server.handler,
        "127.0.0.1",
        0,
        process_request=server.process_request,
    ) as ws_server:
        port = ws_server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        yield f"127.0.0.1:{port}", server


@pytest_asyncio.fixture
async def server():
    async with running_server() as (addr, srv):
        yield addr, srv


async def http_get(addr: str, path: str) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    def _get():
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://{addr}{path}", timeout=5) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))

    return await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, _get)


async def connect_client(addr: str):
    ws = await websockets.connect(f"ws://{addr}")
    welcome = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    client_id = welcome["payload"]["client_id"]
    return ws, client_id, welcome


async def wait_count(registry, expected: int, timeout: float = 2.0) -> None:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout
    while loop.time() < deadline:
        if registry.count() == expected:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
    raise AssertionError(
        f"registry count never reached {expected}, still {registry.count()}"
    )


async def test_connect_assigns_unique_ids(server):
    addr, srv = server
    ws1, id1, welcome1 = await connect_client(addr)
    ws2, id2, welcome2 = await connect_client(addr)
    assert id1 != id2
    assert welcome1["type"] == "system"

    await ws2.close()

    ws1, _, _ = await connect_client(addr)
    ws2, _, _ = await connect_client(addr)

    status, body = await http_get(addr, "/health")
    assert status == 200
    assert body["connected_clients"] == 2

    await ws1.close()
    await ws2.close()
    await wait_count(srv.registry, 0)

    status, body = await http_get(addr, "/health")
    assert status == 200
    assert body["connected_clients"] == 0

    with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as exc:

# ── Transport layer ────────────────────────────────────────────────

class BaseTransport(abc.ABC):
    """
    Abstract transport interface for client connections.

    Concrete transports (WebSocket, SSE, polling, raw TCP) plug the
    connection-level mechanics into the :class:`NotificationServer` so the core
    logic never depends on how messages reach a client. A transport owns each
    client's connection object; the server keeps track of client identity,
    channel subscriptions and message routing.

    Implementations are registered with a name (``__init_subclass__``) and
    selected through the ``TRANSPORT`` environment variable, defaulting to
    ``"websocket"``.
    """

    _factories: dict[str, type["BaseTransport"]] = {}

    def __init_subclass__(
        cls, name: str | None = None, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
        if name:
            cls._factories[name] = cls

    def __init__(self, server: "NotificationServer") -> None:
        self.server = server

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def on_connect(self, connection) -> None:
        """Drive the full lifecycle of a single client connection."""

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def on_disconnect(self, client_id: str) -> None:
        """Clean up server state after a client disconnects."""

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def send_message(self, client_id: str, message: str) -> bool:
        """Deliver a serialized message. Return False if the client is gone."""

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def broadcast(self, message: str) -> None:
        """Deliver a serialized message to every connected client."""


class WebSocketTransport(BaseTransport, name="websocket"):
    """Transport built on the ``websockets`` library (the default)."""

    async def on_connect(self, websocket) -> None:
        server = self.server
        await server._ensure_listener()
        client_id = server._new_client_id()
        server.registry.add(client_id, websocket)
        await server.connection_store.register(client_id)
        welcome = make_message(
            "system",
            {"client_id": client_id, "message": "connected"},
        )
        try:
            await websocket.send(json.dumps(welcome))
            async for raw in websocket:
                await server._handle_message(client_id, raw)
        except ConnectionClosed:
            pass
        finally:
            await self.on_disconnect(client_id)

    async def on_disconnect(self, client_id: str) -> None:
        server = self.server
        server.registry.remove(client_id)
        server.channels.remove_client(client_id)
        await server._sync_channel_subscriptions()
        await server.connection_store.unregister(client_id)

    async def send_message(self, client_id: str, message: str) -> bool:
        websocket = self.server.registry.get(client_id)
        if websocket is None:
            return False
        try:
            await websocket.send(message)
        except ConnectionClosed:
            return False
        return True

    async def broadcast(self, message: str) -> None:
        for client_id, _ in list(self.server.registry.all()):
            await self.send_message(client_id, message)


def _make_transport(server: "NotificationServer") -> BaseTransport:
    """Build the transport named by the ``TRANSPORT`` env var (default websocket)."""
    name = os.environ.get("TRANSPORT", "websocket").strip().lower()
    try:
        factory = BaseTransport._factories[name]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown transport: {name!r}; available: "
            + ", ".join(sorted(BaseTransport._factories))
        )
    return factory(server)
